title: Signal Assembler: Sales/CS enterprise request bundling and first-pass scoping
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Sales and CS regularly surface enterprise feature asks that overlap or are subsets of existing roadmap work. Currently requests arrive as disparate tickets, one-off emails, or Slack threads. This creates context loss, duplicate work, and slow scoping cycles for high-value accounts.

Goal: Build a repeatable, lightweight 'Signal Assembler' process that aggregates enterprise feature requests into coherent bundles, applies an account-weighted initial value and feasibility score, produces a one-page quick-scope, and routes prioritized bundles to PM/Eng for deeper scoping or to Solutions for pilot work. The process should be usable by CS/Sales reps with minimal friction (15–30 min per bundle) and produce artifacts that reduce follow-up discovery by 40%.

Core outputs: 1) Aggregated request bundle (account, signals from multiple contacts, ask summary). 2) Value density score (see scoring formula below). 3) Initial tech-risk & compliance flags. 4) Quick-scope template (problem, acceptance criteria, major non-functional constraints, suggested dev bucket S/M/L). 5) Triage decision: Backlog / Candidate for Pilot / Escalate to Roadmap.

Why this approach: Aggregation reduces duplicate signals; account-weighting prioritizes strategic revenue motions; a lightweight quick-scope reduces back-and-forth and improves handoffs between GTM and Product/Eng. This sits upstream of our existing enterprise intake playbooks but emphasizes fast, consistent scoping for inbound sales/CS asks.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical Signal Assembler playbook doc exists in Confluence and is linked to the Sales/CS intake hub.
A one-page quick-scope template (Google Drive) is published and can be completed in <= 30 minutes by a CS rep.
Pilot: CS completes 5 bundles with the template; we measure time to triage and reduction in follow-up questions.
A simple dashboard (spreadsheet or GA) shows aggregated requests weekly and top 10 account-weighted bundles.
Clear handoff handshake with Eng/Platform (required fields mapped to ENG intake ticket format).
steps: Step 1: CS/Sales identifies related asks across account — collect signal sources (PRs, emails, conversations).
Step 2: Use quick-scope template: summarize problem, user persona, ROI hypothesis, acceptance criteria, security/compliance notes, suggested dev bucket (S/M/L).
Step 3: Compute 'value density' = (Estimated ARR influence * Account weight) / Dev bucket size; map to High/Medium/Low.
Step 4: Apply feasibility flags: infra risk, data residency, KMS/HSM requirement, private deployment needs. Mark as 'requires security review' if any compliance flags present.
Step 5: Create aggregated bundle record in intake sheet and tag with owner (CS rep), recommended next step (Backlog / Pilot / Roadmap Escalation).
Step 6: Weekly triage sync: PMs review top 10 bundles; select 1–2 for deeper discovery or pilot handoff.
Step 7: Track outcomes: accepted to roadmap, pilot launched, deprioritized; record time-to-triage and follow-up question count.
decision_log: 2025-02-12 — Decided to use account-weighted scoring vs raw count to prioritize strategic accounts (PM consensus).
2025-02-20 — Chose a quick-scope template limited to one page to keep friction low (Design feedback: keep fields minimal).
2025-02-25 — Agreed that security_review_required should be flagged in the template; actual security sign-off not required for initial triage (Security input).
2025-03-01 — Pilot with EMEA CS team approved; scope = 5 bundles over 3 weeks before broader rollout (GTM lead sign-off).
notes: Trade-offs: a stricter template improves consistency but increases friction for CS. We intentionally prioritize speed over completeness for first-pass triage.
We will not change core roadmap prioritization rules in this project; Signal Assembler feeds the PM queue with higher-quality inputs but does not override roadmap decisions.
Consider building an automated bundling helper in the future that clusters asks by title/keywords (engineering backlog idea).
Account-weighting approach: weight = 1 + min(4, floor(ARR_bucket_multiplier)). We'll calibrate buckets after 10 pilot bundles.
